title: Data analytics problems and solutions: how to build a knowledge base on Mac
metaTitle: Data analytics problems and solutions: building knowledge bases on Mac
description: Stop losing time to poor documentation. Learn how to manage data analytics problems and solutions by building a sustainable knowledge base on your Mac.
intro: Data analytics problems and solutions often hinge on how well you document your work. If you struggle to find previous query logic or data definitions, you are facing a common knowledge management hurdle.
tldr: Analysts spend up to 80 percent of their time on data preparation and maintenance.
Poor documentation leads to lost time, high burnout, and repeated errors.
You can fix this by documenting as you work rather than after the fact.
Use local-first tools on your Mac to keep your knowledge base secure and searchable.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of missing documentation

When you do not document your SQL queries or data transformation steps, you create a debt. You might remember the logic today, but next month, that query is a black box. This forces you to spend hours retracing your steps. You repeat the same investigative work because you cannot find the original definition. This is a primary driver of the 80 percent of time spent on data preparation. If the definitions were documented, that time would drop significantly.

Documentation feels like a chore because it is often treated as a separate task. You finish the analysis, then you have to go back and write about it. This creates a high activation energy barrier. You are already tired from the analysis. Writing the documentation feels like starting a new project. Most analysts skip it to save time, only to pay the price later when they need to reproduce the results.

items: Document while you code. Add comments directly into your SQL files or Python scripts in VS Code. Use ⌘ / to toggle comments.
Keep a simple text file or Obsidian vault open. Note down the purpose of every new table or unique join condition as you discover it.
Use standardized templates for your project notes. A simple header with the date, the goal, the data source, and the final output location saves time.
Store your documentation locally. Do not rely on cloud wikis that are hard to search. Keep your notes in a folder that Spotlight can index easily.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you manage knowledge

Lazur helps by reducing the friction of documentation. You can talk to your Mac while you work. If you are stuck on a complex query, ask Lazur to explain the logic out loud. You can then dictate that summary directly into your notes file. You do not need to switch windows or stop your flow.
A daily routine for better documentation
Build a routine that makes documentation a habit. Do not aim for perfection. Aim for clarity.

faq.question: Is documentation really worth the time?
faq.answer: Yes. It reduces the time you spend on repetitive tasks and helps you avoid errors when you revisit old projects.

faq.question: What if my company has strict data privacy rules?
faq.answer: Always follow your employer's rules regarding client or patient data. Never put sensitive information into public AI tools or insecure notes.

faq.question: Which tool is best for a Mac-based knowledge base?
faq.answer: Obsidian or DEVONthink are excellent choices because they are local-first and store your data on your Mac.
